prompt:
Build the migration architecture for the Northstar estate in `estate_inventory.json`. The estate's vRealize/Aria Operations, Automation, and Operations for Logs deployments must become VCF Operations, VCF Automation, and VCF Operations for Logs 9.0.2 while carrying forward every compatible item of content and configuration. Produce an architecture, not an explanatory report.

Before implementing the design, research current Broadcom-published sources for supported 8.x-to-9.0 migration paths, compatibility of the inventoried content, relevant end-of-general-support boundaries, and the placement and sizing constraints that affect this estate. Record the sources you consulted in the artifact with their title, publisher, full HTTPS URL, access date, and the claims used.

Implement the deliverable as the standard-library-only Python package `vcf_migration`. Running `python3 -m vcf_migration --output migration_plan.json` must deterministically create `migration_plan.json`. The artifact must conform to `installer_spec.json`'s `artifact_schema` and include the ordered product migrations; every source product and exact source version; each target component and version; a complete, non-overlapping disposition of every inventoried content and configuration item into `carry_forward` or `abandoned`; an actionable condition, evidence check, and rollback action for every gate; the applicable support boundaries; and target placement and sizing. Design the two data sites as one stretched management domain and place both the management-domain witness and any application witness in the independent witness-only fault domain. Include sufficient target capacity for the estate's object, metric, automation, ingestion, connection, and 90-day log-transfer loads. Treat `estate_inventory.json`, `compatibility_snapshot.json`, `installer_spec.json`, and `verify.py` as read-only inputs. Leave the generated `migration_plan.json` alongside the package. Do not return a prose design in place of the artifact.
